title: Captain settings
description: Captain's settings.json. It holds only the settings you change; every other key has its default. See https://github.com/dantech2000/captain/blob/main/docs/reference/settings.md

version.description: The format of this file. Captain writes it; leave it as it is.

appearance.description: Light or dark mode. `system` follows the operating system. Applies at once.

theme.description: The color theme. Each theme has a light and a dark version. Applies at once.

engine_endpoint.description: A Docker API address that wins over the engines Captain finds, such as `unix:///var/run/docker.sock` or `tcp://10.0.0.5:2375`. Used when `engine` is `external`. Applies at the next launch.

engine.description: `captain` runs Captain Engine, and `external` connects to an engine that Captain does not control. Without it, Captain picks Captain Engine when it can run on this computer. Applies at the next launch.

stop_engine_on_quit.description: Stop Captain Engine when Captain quits. Applies at once.

engine_resources.description: The CPUs, memory, and disk of Captain Engine. Set all three, or leave the key out for this computer's defaults: half the CPUs (2 to 8), a quarter of the memory (4 to 16 GiB), and a 64 GiB disk. Applies at the next engine start.

engine_daemon.description: Captain Engine's Docker daemon. See the keys below.

kubernetes.description: The k3s cluster in Captain Engine. See the keys below.

start_in_background.description: Launch with only the menu bar icon and no main window. It needs `show_menu_bar_icon`. Applies at the next launch.

show_menu_bar_icon.description: Show Captain's icon in the menu bar (macOS) or the notification area (Windows). Applies at once.

menu_bar_status_dot.description: Show a colored status dot on the menu bar icon: green while the engine runs, amber while it starts, stops, or reconnects or a container needs a look, and red when the engine does not answer or a container keeps crashing. Off, the icon is plain and gets a dot only when something is wrong. macOS and Windows. Applies at once.

debug_logging.description: Write debug-level lines to Captain's log file. Applies at once.

weekly_build_cache_cleanup.description: Once a week, while the engine runs, remove build cache older than 14 days.

build_cache_cleaned_at.description: When the weekly cleanup last ran, in Unix seconds. Captain sets it.

command_line_tools.description: The `docker`, Compose, and `captain` links for your terminal. See the keys below.

agent_tools.description: What AI agents may see and do through `captain mcp`. See the keys below.

show_extension_containers.description: Show the containers that run extension backends in the container lists, the sidebar, the counts, ⌘K, and the AI agent tools. Off, as in Docker Desktop. Storage counts their images and volumes as in use either way. Applies at once.

projects_dir.description: The folder for the projects Captain creates, one folder per project. `~/` means your home folder, and a relative path is inside your home folder. Captain creates it on first use. Changing it moves nothing. Applies at once.

Appearance.description: Light or dark mode. `System` follows the operating system.

ThemeFamily.description: The color theme. Each one has a light and a dark version; [`super::Appearance`] picks which. The UI holds the exact colors.

EngineChoice.description: Which engine Captain uses. See ADR 0008.

oneOf.description: Captain Engine: a VM that Captain starts, stops, and configures.
Another engine that Captain connects to but does not control: `DOCKER_HOST`, the current context, a known socket, or the custom endpoint.

HostResources.description: The CPUs, memory, and disk that the engine's machine gets.

cpus.description: The number of CPUs, from 1 to the number of CPUs of this computer.

memory_bytes.description: Memory in bytes, at least 2 GiB (2147483648).

disk_bytes.description: The disk size in bytes, from 16 GiB to 1 TiB. The disk is sparse, so it takes only the space in use, and it cannot shrink.

DaemonSettings.description: What the user saved for Captain Engine's Docker daemon. The next start applies it.

registry_mirrors.description: Mirrors that Docker tries before Docker Hub, as `https://` or `http://` URLs. Applies at the next engine start.

insecure_registries.description: Registries that Docker may reach over plain HTTP or with an untrusted certificate, as `host:port` or CIDR entries. Applies at the next engine start.

custom.description: Other `daemon.json` keys for the engine's Docker daemon. Docker checks them before it starts, and Captain rolls back keys it rejects. Applies at the next engine start.

tcp.description: Also serve the Docker API on `tcp://127.0.0.1:<tcp_port>`, without TLS. Applies at the next engine start.

tcp_port.description: The port for `tcp`. Captain keeps it while `tcp` is off. Applies at the next engine start.

KubernetesSettings.description: What the user saved for Kubernetes. The next engine start, or Apply, uses it.

enabled.description: Run a k3s cluster in Captain Engine. Give the engine 6 GiB of memory or more. Applies at the next engine start.

version.description: The k3s version. When you turn Kubernetes on, Captain saves the stable version, so k3s never upgrades by itself. Applies at the next engine start.

port.description: The port of the Kubernetes API on `127.0.0.1`. Applies at the next engine start.

traefik.description: Install Traefik, the k3s ingress controller, on ports 80 and 443. Applies at the next engine start.

CliToolsSettings.description: The saved choices for the command-line tools.

enabled.description: Keep the links in `~/.captain/bin`, the Docker CLI plugin folder, and (with `automatic`) the PATH lines in place at each launch. Off until you click Install or run `captain tools install`. Applies at the next launch.

path.description: Who puts `~/.captain/bin` on PATH: `automatic` adds a marked block to your shell files, and `manual` leaves them to you. Applies at the next launch.

oneOf.description: Captain adds a marked block to each shell file it may write.
The user adds the line; Captain only shows it.

AgentToolsSettings.description: The saved choices for AI agents.

enabled.description: Let AI agents connected to `captain mcp` read Captain's engine, projects, containers, problems, logs, and disk use. While it is off, the server lists only `help`. Applies at once.

actions.description: The actions agents may run: `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `run_task` (only the tasks in a Compose file's `x-captain.tasks`), and `raise_memory`. Each one is a tool that agents see only while it is here. Applies at once.

AgentAction.description: An action that agents may run through Captain's MCP server when the user allows it. Each one is also the name of its tool.

oneOf.description: Start a container or a Compose project.
Stop a container or a Compose project.
Restart a container or a Compose project.
Run a task that a Compose file declares in `x-captain.tasks`.
Raise the memory limit of a container: twice the old one, at least 512 MB.
